title: GitHub - komovaar/kolo: Multiplayer AI coding agents. One machine runs them, everybody else opens a link.
excerpt: Multiplayer AI coding agents. One machine runs them, everybody else opens a link. - komovaar/kolo
content_html:
Multiplayer AI coding agents.

Run agents on one machine and work together in the browser. Share a link so your team can watch, type, and take over the same session. Only the host installs Kolo.

Why Kolo

  • Work in the same session. Everyone sees the same terminal. Type a prompt, approve a step, or pick up where a teammate left off.
  • Bring your terminal agents. Built-in adapters for Claude Code, Codex CLI, and opencode, with custom agent descriptions for other tools.
  • Give observers a seat. Read-only members can follow along while the host decides who can control sessions.

Quick start

Kolo is an experimental alpha for trusted teams. Agents run with the host user's permissions. Start in a dedicated VM with only the projects and credentials you intend to share; see the isolation setup.

Install on the machine that will run the agents:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/komovaar/kolo/main/install | KOLO_VERSION=v0.1.0 sh

Then open a project and start Kolo:

cd /path/to/project
kolo up

Send your team the invitation link printed in the terminal. They open it in a browser, choose a name, and join. No install or token to paste.

Hosts support Linux and macOS on amd64 and arm64. Use WSL2 on Windows. For rolling development builds, replace v0.1.0 with nightly.

How it works

One Go binary runs the hub your team opens and the host that starts agents. kolo up runs both together. Use kolo serve and kolo host to run them on separate machines. Hosts connect out to the hub; the hub needs to be reachable from your team's browsers.

Kolo detects agent status from terminal output, so CLI updates can affect status and resume behavior. Run kolo doctor to check your setup, and see tested versions and limits for current compatibility.

Documentation

Start with kolo help or kolo help <command>.
